mathematics.independent_solution: Outside a neutral infinite steady-current wire B is nonzero and E=0. The invariant B^2-E^2/c^2 is positive, so no inertial transformation can make B vanish there. In an electron-comoving frame the positive ions still carry current; the electric field may become nonzero.

E'=B'=0 would make the invariant zero, contradicting its positive value.

Changing n from z to (x+y)/sqrt(2) changes E_y from zero to nonzero.

mathematics.independent_solution: In a nonzero free-space plane wave B=(n cross E)/c. For E along x and n=y, B is along -z, the same oscillation line as z. For n=(y+z)/sqrt(2), B is along (y-z)/sqrt(2). E along x cannot coexist with n=x because E must be transverse.

option_checks.evidence: An unmarked antenna shape alone gives neither incident polarization nor propagation nor matching.
y cross x=-z; sign reversal during oscillation leaves the vertical oscillation line unchanged.
(y+z) cross x=y-z; B is oblique rather than universally vertical.
Nonzero E parallel to n violates transversality; n cross E would be zero, not the stipulated wave.

mathematics.independent_solution: For n=y, B_I=(E0/c)*cos(phi)*(x-z)/sqrt(2); B_II=(E0/c)*(x*sin(phi)-z*cos(phi)), of constant nonzero magnitude rotating in the xz plane. Axial drives E_I dot x=E0*cos(phi)/sqrt(2) and E_II dot x=E0*cos(phi) are alternating and not identically zero. Their zeros at isolated phases do not eliminate reception.

B_I is along x-z, not x+z; the latter is its E direction and is not perpendicular to E_I.
